subject: POC capacity planning - HexaTech (post-call recap & next steps)
snippet: Recap from today's call: agree success criteria, reserved GPUs for baseline, autoscaling policy for bursts, and proposed timeline for a 4-week POC.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@hexatech.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning - HexaTech (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I send the formal POC proposal: 

Summary of what we agreed on during the call:
- Success criteria: 95th percentile inference latency < 200ms for 512-token responses (chat), end-to-end throughput to support ~120 RPS peak across 3 concurrent evaluation pipelines, and qualitatively acceptable answer fidelity on the 50-case eval set your team will run.
- Ownership: HexaTech owns eval dataset and acceptance signoff; Redwood provides runtime, capacity plan, and onboarding support.
- Timeline: 4-week POC starting the week of July 6 (tentative). Week 0 (kickoff/onboarding), Week 1 baseline runs, Week 2 optimizations, Week 3 final eval and handover.

Capacity items we discussed you wanted captured explicitly:
1) Reserved capacity: baseline reserved pool of 4 x A100-40GB (expected to cover steady-state throughput for your sample traffic and give consistent latency).
2) Autoscaling: allow burst autoscaling up to 8 GPUs for short periods (up to 30 minutes per hour) for load tests and peak demos. Autoscaler policy to prefer local reserved pool first, then burst from shared capacity.
3) Burst expectations: cold-start to additional instances ~45-60s for new nodes; we recommend synthetic warm-up before critical demos.
4) Cost controls: apply soft cap alerts at 60% of burst limit and hard guardrails if you want to limit costs during tests.

Next steps I propose from Redwood:
- I'll share a formal POC proposal (capacity + pricing + SOW) by EOW (Friday). Attachment will include the capacity playbook and a suggested rollout plan.
- HexaTech to confirm acceptance criteria (the 50-case eval set + any additional metrics) and provide a sample of the eval data (anonymized) by Tuesday.
- Schedule kickoff for week of July 6 if we have approvals by July 2.

See attached: hexatech_poc_proposal.pdf (draft) and redwood_poc_capacity_playbook.xlsx.

If that aligns, I'll finalize the proposal and loop in your procurement contact.

Best,
Marissa

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - HexaTech (post-call recap & next steps)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria: we will run the 50-case eval plus a 1-hour soak test at ~100 RPS to validate stability. We'll sign off if latency and qualitative checks pass across both runs.
2) Reserved GPUs: 4 x A100 sounds right for baseline. Can you confirm whether those are dedicated instances (no noisy neighbors) or reserved shared capacity? We prefer isolated machines for the POC.
3) Autoscaling: 8 GPUs burst is fine. For the soak test we'll want to reserve 2x for sustained traffic, so please include a policy that supports a temporary sustained increase for soak windows up to 2 hours if needed.
4) Compliance: procurement will request SOC2 and data handling notes as part of the SOW — we'll send the procurement contact once you share the proposal.

We'll aim to get the eval dataset to you by Tuesday EOD.

Aisha
VP Product
HexaTech Labs
aisha@hexatech.ai

Hi Aisha, thanks for the quick turnaround and helpful notes. A couple of clarifications and the proposed final POC capacity plan below: 

1) Dedicated vs reserved: For the POC we can provide Dedicated (isolated) instances for the reserved pool — we'll mark the 4 x A100-40GB as dedicated reserved nodes for your account. That meets your 'noisy neighbor' requirement.

2) Autoscaling & soak window: We'll configure autoscaling as follows:
- Baseline reserved pool: 4 x A100-40GB (dedicated)
- Autoscale target: scale up to 8 x A100-40GB for bursts
- Burst policy: up to 30 minutes per hour by default; we will include an option to extend to 2-hour soak windows during scheduled tests. Soak windows must be scheduled (simple API call or calendar invite) to avoid unexpected billing spikes.
- Warm-up recommendation: pre-warm the KV cache and run a 10-minute synthetic warm-up at 0.25 RPS per endpoint before critical demos to reduce effective cold-start impact.

3) Cost/alerts: we'll set soft alerts at 60% GPU utilization and a hard budget cap tied to your HubSpot deal that triggers an auto-notify to procurement. We'll include a suggested billing estimate in the proposal.

4) Role summary: 
- HexaTech: provide eval dataset, acceptance signoff, procurement contact
- Redwood: provision dedicated reserved capacity, implement autoscale policy, onboarding and 2x office hours/week during POC, final report at the end of the POC

5) Timeline: Kickoff July 6 if approvals on July 2. Full 4-week plan attached.

If that aligns I'll update the proposal and send a DocuSign SOW and the procurement package.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: hexatech_poc_proposal.pdf (updated)
